correctness.rationale: Orthogonal kernel derived directly from variance and independence. The finite C(Ω) operator norm is an absolute kernel-row maximum. A centered common-corner variable is supported inside the rare-corner variable’s two endpoints, so the rare variable dominates it in convex order; independent-coordinate replacement gives a global rare-corner maximum. At that vertex the kernel becomes a centered rare-Bernoulli weighted sum. The homogeneous binomial boundary follows by exact signed-mass telescoping, and the two limits by local CLT/Poisson convergence. Exact-rational full-kernel tests matched 2,286 homogeneous and 1,860 heterogeneous rows, plus 4,455 support formula comparisons; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical first-order Fourier/Hoeffding orthogonal projection is useful for truncating bounded product-cube functions. A new coordinatewise convex-order principle collapses an exponentially large row extremization to a unique explicit rare-corner distribution for every nonidentical bias vector. The derived exact one-binomial-boundary homogeneous law reveals a sharp Gaussian-to-Poisson scaling transition in sup norm, inaccessible from the existing uniform Haar projection-constant formula. The theorem concerns a natural operator, not an arbitrary tailored numerical slice.
